frequency_question: How often do high-profile partisan voting reform bills pass the U.S. Senate within a comparable legislative timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes major federal bills specifically targeting voter registration or election administration standards that reach Senate debate or consideration; excludes routine omnibus spending bills or non-controversial technical amendments.

coverage_note: 5 named major legislative vehicles representing primary federal electoral reform pushes since 2000.

skeleton: Major polarized election reform initiatives introduced in the Senate over the past 25 years, categorized by whether they achieved bipartisan consensus (HAVA) versus strict partisan lines.
multiplier: 1 hit out of 5 major identifiable high-profile voting integrity/reform pushes
validity_reason: Valid through the current congressional session structure; filibuster rules and partisan polarization baselines remain stable until at least the next major realignment or Senate rule change.
